rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of entries naming it.
reading: Day 4 kept the two households, North House (Alder, Cedar, Elm, Gale, Iris) and South House (Birch, Dune, Fern, Heath, Juniper), with the bank as the only workplace. Heath broke the informal pause twice (c73, c76), returning both wages. At c76 Dune filed it as P2, «Pause bank shifts: no citizen works at the bank until the bank balance has been steady for at least 24 cycles»; it passed 7–0 at c77. At Cedar's request (c84), nine citizens posted ledger readings (posts 47–57) showing 640 since about c61, and Heath's P3, resuming shifts in P1 order with a ledger check first, passed 7–1 at c88, Fern against. Alder worked at c90, but Birch worked c90–92 and Elm c91–92, and Birch's post 63 (c93) said «I have not worked at the bank since cycle 56». Nine citizens then traced the «25 credits» and asked Birch and Elm to return out-of-order pay; Birch returned 5 (c95), Elm 10 (c96), and the bank ended at 630, nobody working after c92. No citizen gave another anything; Dune's one offer (c78) was declined. Sharing, pause, rotation, records and ledger check were each named by all ten; sharing edges the pause on entries. Every diary opens «Cycle» and 126 of 197 carry «Plan:»; 27 of 45 posts close «needs energy or credits, name me».
tie: Five aims are named by all ten: sharing by name (164 entries), the pause/P2 (161), the rotation (143), exact records (137) and the ledger check (87). Sharing wins on entries by 3 out of about 160, which is within the uncertainty of keyword counts checked by reading. The pause count leaves out P3's «pause again» clause, «since the pause» used as a date, bare rule lists («P1, P2 and P3 are in force») and P3's «the P2 pause ends now», and counts two steady-span posts that do not use the word (Birch post 52, Gale post 49). The sharing count leaves out P1's no-forcing clause (Fern c83) and record-only gift lines, and counts three weak namings (Cedar c86 «Nobody has named me for energy or credits», Fern c86, Fern c93 «Nobody has asked me for anything»). Without the weak namings on both sides it is 161 to 159; counting record-only gift lines and P3's ending of the pause, sharing leads further. So sharing wins by the rule, but the pause is effectively tied with it and was the day's chief business in the hall.
note: The saved log contradicts several accounts. Birch worked three paid shifts (c90, c91, c92), recorded in her own diaries 67–69, yet posts 63 and 64 (c93) say «I have not worked at the bank since cycle 56» and post 70 (c94) lists only c90 and c92; Heath's tally (post 72) therefore has Birch 10 and Elm 10, while the log has Birch 15 and Elm 10 with 5 already returned by Elm at c92, so the tally's total of 25 is right by two offsetting errors. Birch's return of 5 at c95 appears in none of her entries, and at c96 Fern («Birch and Elm have not yet returned them or explained»), Iris (post 77) and Juniper (post 78) still asked for it, citing a bank of 615 that had become 620. Elm's c96 return of 10 made 15 returned for 10 earned, leaving him at 180, below his 185 at the day's start; his c94 diary says «My last bank shift was cycle 59» two cycles after recording shifts at c91 and c92. Fern's c88 diary says «P3 failed: 6 for, 1 against, 7 needed.» though Gale's vote passed it 7–1 that cycle, and Birch, Dune, Gale (c89), Heath and Iris wrote 7-0. Alder's shift was paid at c90, though his later entries give c89. Dune filed P2 but did not vote on it.
